{{Quote|I suppose I should ask after my niece. She's done well for herself, though I admit she and I have lost touch since you spirited her away from us.|Arkoh Adasca, to Lucien Draay|<ref name="KOTOR 19" />}}
'''Aurora Adasca''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the niece of [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Arkoh Adasca]], head of the [[The Adasca BioMechanical Corporation of Arkania|Adasca Corporation]]. She became a [[Jedi scout|scout]] for the [[Revanchist]] movement on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Serroco]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]] but was left unaccounted for after [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] [[Battle of Serroco|attacked]] the planet in [[3963 BBY]].

==Biography==
The niece of [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Arkoh Adasca]], the head of [[The Adasca BioMechanical Corporation of Arkania]], Aurora Adasca was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] who lived in the period of [[Time/Legends|time]] that followed the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. As she was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], Aurora was taken by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for [[Jedi training/Legends|training]],<ref name="CSWE" /> an action her uncle likened to an abduction. Arkoh Adasca never contacted her after she was taken, nor did [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Lucien Draay]]&mdash;a family friend of the [[House of Adasca|Adascas]]&mdash;ever see her again, either.<ref name="KOTOR 19" /> Aurora eventually became a [[Jedi scout]] and traveled to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Serroco]] to assist the [[Revanchist]] movement, which aimed to involve the whole Order in the ongoing [[Mandalorian Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]].<ref name="DHCb" /> After Serroco was [[Battle of Serroco|razed]] by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] in [[3963 BBY]], Aurora was left unaccounted for. As she was the sole remaining heir to the House of Adasca after her uncle was [[First Battle of Omonoth|killed]], her disappearance enabled investors of the [[Draay Trust]] to bid for the takeover of the Adasca Corporation.<ref name="TAL" />

==Behind the scenes==
Aurora Adasca was first mentioned in the [[Knights of the Old Republic 19|nineteenth issue]] of the [[Dark Horse Comics|Dark Horse]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic-book]] series [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'']]. The issue was written by [[John Jackson Miller]]<ref name="KOTOR 19" /> and published on [[August 22]], [[2007]].<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54338/star_wars_knights_of_the_old_republic_2006_19|text=Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (2006) #19}}</ref> It was not until [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' that the character was named.<ref name="CSWE" />

In [[John Ostrander]]'s early outlines for ''[[Star Wars: Vector]]'', the lead protagonist was intended to be an Arkanian Jedi named Aurora. As such, John Jackson Miller planted the character of Aurora Adasca in the nineteenth issue of ''Knights of the Old Republic'' in anticipation for the character's future appearance. However, plans for ''Vector'' ended up changing and the lead protagonist was instead a [[Human/Legends|human]] Jedi named [[Celeste Morne]].<ref name="KOTOR Countdown">{{Faraway|url=2010/02/15/kotor-countdown-4-lady-vanishes-or|text=KOTOR Countdown #4: The Lady Vanishes — or, The Mystery of Aurora}}</ref>
